about: What fails around the code: the tools, the services, the tests and the pipeline. Each row says how to recognise the failure, its cause and the next step. `family` is the kind the diagnoser gives it: transient, environment, code, test or spec.

rows.title: Failure: `nuclear`, `dragonfly` or `nuclear-loop`: command not found
rows.summary: The tool is not installed, or it is not on the PATH of the program that ran it (an editor started from the desktop does not have `~/.local/bin`). Install with the installer or `./install.sh`, and check with `dragonfly doctor`.
body: **Looks like.** `nuclear: command not found`, `dragonfly is not installed (run the NuclearLang installer)`, exit code 127.
**Cause.** The binaries live in `~/.local/bin`. A terminal has that folder on its PATH; a desktop program may not.

**Next step.** `which nuclear dragonfly nuclear-loop`; install (`curl -fsSL https://nuclearlang.github.io/install.sh | sh`, or `./install.sh` in the source tree); add `~/.local/bin` to the PATH; `dragonfly doctor` lists what else is missing. The Loop adds the installers' folders by itself.
asks: the terminal says dragonfly is not a command

rows.title: Failure: the installed tools are older than the source tree
rows.summary: A command, a kind or a diagnostic that exists in the sources is unknown to the installed binary, or the editor reports an error the terminal does not: the installed copy is stale. Run `./install.sh` again after changing the compiler, a dialect or the CLI.
body: **Looks like.** `dragonfly: unknown command`, a kind the docs describe is `N0201`, the editor and `nuclear check` disagree, a Python package of a folder dependency behaves like an old version.
**Cause.** `nuclear`, `dragonfly`, the language server and the editors' bundled copies are installed copies; a project's folder dependency is installed into its `build/.venv`.
**Next step.** `./install.sh` (it rebuilds and reinstalls everything); in a project, `dragonfly install` reinstalls folder dependencies. Restart the editor to load the new server.

rows.title: Failure: the Nuclear Smart Graph is not reachable
rows.summary: A search, an ingest or an agent's recall cannot connect to `127.0.0.1:7878`: the graph's server is not running. Start its service again (`nuclear-loop setup --status` says what is down); an agent that cannot reach it goes on without knowledge and says so in its trace.
body: **Looks like.** `the graph is not running at http://127.0.0.1:7878`, `the Nuclear Smart Graph is not reachable`, `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:7878`, `connection refused`.
**Cause.** `nuclear-graph serve` is not running, or it listens on another port (`NUCLEAR_GRAPH_PORT`, `NUCLEAR_GRAPH_URL`). Its embeddings also need Ollama with the model `embeddinggemma`.

**Next step.** `nuclear-loop setup --status`; then restart the service: `systemctl --user restart nuclear-graph` on Linux, `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/io.github.nuclearlang.graph` on macOS, or the settings page of VS Code (`Ctrl+Alt+S`). A machine never set up: `nuclear-loop setup`. By hand: `nuclear-graph serve &`. Then `nuclear-graph stats` (the rows of each shelf and the revision). It is a passing failure: a run retries it by itself.

rows.title: Failure: a program has no access to the graph (401, 403)
rows.summary: The graph answers 401 (no token) or 403 (the token lacks a scope): no program reads it until you allow it. Give the client access with `nuclear-graph connect <client> --scopes read,write`, or allow its pending request.
body: **Looks like.** `'mcp' has no access to the Nuclear Smart Graph: run nuclear-graph connect mcp`, `401 a token is needed`, `403 client 'x' has no 'write' scope`.
**Cause.** Each client has its own token, kept in your keyring, with scopes: `read` (search, prompts), `write` (remember, examples), `admin` (ingest: only the owner).

**Next step.** `nuclear-graph connect nuclear-developer --scopes read,write` (the local agents), `nuclear-graph connect mcp --scopes read,write` (the MCP server); `nuclear-graph requests` shows who asked; `nuclear-graph allow <request>`. Restart the client so it reads its token.

**The keyring was closed.** A graph that starts at login runs before the keyring opens: it waits for it (its log says `the keyring that keeps the graph's `owner` is closed` when it gives up, and the service starts again by itself). A graph of before 2026-11-13 made a second owner's token instead and answered 401 to your own commands until it was restarted: `systemctl --user restart nuclear-graph`.

rows.title: Failure: the Nuclear Developer is not running
rows.summary: A stage of the Loop, the chat or an MCP tool cannot reach the local agents at `127.0.0.1:7879`. Start their service again (`nuclear-loop setup --status` says what is down); a run checks it before it starts and retries a passing failure with growing waits.
body: **Looks like.** `the local developer is not running at http://127.0.0.1:7879`, `fetch failed`, a run that stops at its preflight step.

**Next step.** `nuclear-loop setup --status`; then `systemctl --user restart nuclear-developer` on Linux (`journalctl --user -u nuclear-developer -n 50` says why it stopped), `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/io.github.nuclearlang.developer` on macOS, or the settings page of VS Code. A machine never set up: `nuclear-loop setup`. By hand: `nuclear-developer &`; another port: `NUCLEAR_DEVELOPER_PORT`, `NUCLEAR_DEVELOPER_URL`. Then `nuclear-loop retry <run>`: the steps that passed are kept.

rows.title: Failure: the set-up stops because a service started by hand answers on its port
rows.summary: The set-up of the AI services stops at *Start the Smart Graph* (or *the Nuclear Developer*) with `a ... started by hand already answers at ...`: a graph or a Developer started in a terminal holds the port, so the system's service cannot take it. Stop that process with the command the message gives and try the step again.
body: **Looks like.** `a Nuclear Smart Graph started by hand already answers at http://127.0.0.1:7878/v1/health: stop it (pkill -f 'nuclear-graph serve') and run the set-up again, so the service of this system takes its place`.

**Cause.** Before the set-up existed the services were started with `nuclear-graph serve &` and `nuclear-developer &`. Such a process keeps running old code and is gone after a restart of the machine; the set-up does not kill a process it did not start.

**Next step.** `pkill -f 'nuclear-graph serve'` (the graph) or `pkill -f 'uvicorn app.main:app'` (the Developer); then *Try again* in the wizard, or `nuclear-loop setup --profile <the same> --yes`. A service the editor started (the settings page's *Start*) stops when the editor closes.

rows.title: Failure: Ollama is not running, or a model is not installed
rows.summary: The local agents and the graph's embeddings run on Ollama. When Ollama is down, a model was never pulled, or another program holds the model, calls fail or wait: start Ollama and let the set-up download the models of the machine's profile.
body: **Looks like.** `model 'qwen2.5-coder:3b' not found`, a call that never answers and is cut (*stalled*), `connection refused` on port 11434.

**Next step.** `ollama serve`; `nuclear-loop setup --status` names the models of the profile that are missing, and `nuclear-loop setup` downloads them (by hand: `ollama pull <model>`); `ollama ps` shows which model is loaded and by whom. On a machine with little memory, two programs that load different models make each other wait: let one finish.

rows.title: Failure: a call timed out, or answered 429, 502, 503 or 504
rows.summary: A service was busy or starting. It is a passing failure: the caller retries it with growing waits (five tries by default). When it keeps failing, the service it names is down: start it.
body: **Looks like.** `timed out`, `timeout`, `temporarily unavailable`, a status 408, 425, 429, 502, 503 or 504.

**Next step.** Nothing at first: the Loop retries with exponential backoff (`.nuclear/loop.json`, `retry`). Still failing: see which service the message names (the Developer, the graph, Ollama) and start it; then `nuclear-loop retry <run>`. A compiler error or a failing test is never retried blindly.

rows.title: Failure: the folder is not a Dragonfly project
rows.summary: A `dragonfly` or `nuclear-loop` command finds no `config.nuc` (or `main.nuc`) in the folder or above it. Run it inside a project, or create one with `dragonfly new <name> -p <platform>`.
body: **Looks like.** `no main.nuc or config.nuc in <folder> or above`, `<folder> is not inside a Dragonfly project (no config.nuc)`.
**Next step.** `cd` into the project (the folder that has `config.nuc`), or `--project <dir>`; a new one: `dragonfly new <name> -p backend|mobile|web`.

rows.title: Failure: a package of the generated project is missing
rows.summary: The build ran but the runtime or a package was never installed, or a plugin was enabled after the last install: `ModuleNotFoundError`, `Cannot find module`. Run `dragonfly install` (and `dragonfly build` first when `config.nuc` changed).
body: **Looks like.** `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named ...`, `Cannot find module ...`, `No such file or directory: .venv`.
**Cause.** `build/` carries only the packages of the enabled plugins; they are installed by `dragonfly install`, not by the build.

**Next step.** `dragonfly build && dragonfly install`. For a mobile app that does not build after many changes: `dragonfly repair`. Never install a package by hand inside `build/`: add it in `config.nuc` (`plugins(...)`, `dependencies(...)`).

rows.title: Failure: a test fails
rows.summary: `dragonfly test` reports a failed test. Read it at its `.nuc` lines with `dragonfly explain`, decide whether the code or the test is wrong, fix that file and run again. A test is never deleted or weakened to pass.
body: **Looks like.** `FAILED`, `AssertionError`, `1 failed`, `tests failed`.
**Most common causes.**
- The test reads rows it never created: the database starts empty in every test.
- The code answers another status or value than the criterion says.
- The test kept a `Result` and compared it with a value (`found == 1` instead of `found.value == 1`).
- A call without `~`.
**Next step.** `playbook:fix-a-failing-test`. In the Loop this is the *Verification* stage: three rounds, then the diagnoser explains what is left.

rows.title: Failure: the plan has no pieces
rows.summary: The local planner could not split the spec: it names nothing to build in the platform's words. Name every piece in the spec (a model `Character`, a repository `CharacterRepository`, a use case `ListCharacters`, an appcomponent, a controller), or let a frontier model lead, then restart from the plan.
body: **Looks like.** `0 pieces`, `no pieces`, `the plan does not cover the spec`.
**Cause.** A spec in plain words ("an author has a name; POST /authors adds one") needs someone to decide the names and the files; the local planner splits what a spec says, it does not design.

**Next step.** One sentence per declaration, with its kind word and its name; or give the resource's data (a `GET <url>` line, an example answer) so the generators write it; or `--lead claude`. Then `nuclear-loop retry <run> --from plan`.
keys: plan does not cover the spec

rows.title: Failure: a test or a piece uses a class that is not in the plan
rows.summary: The compiler reports `N0220` for a class of the project that no file declares, and the plan never had it: the plan does not cover the spec. Repairing the file goes in circles; the plan needs the missing piece.
body: **Looks like.** `N0220 'CharactersAppComponent'` on an `inject<...>()`, together with `X is not in the plan`.
**Cause.** The planner made fewer pieces than the feature needs (one entity for a spec that needs a facade and a use case), or the tester copied an example with classes of another project.
**Next step.** Name the missing declaration in the spec, or let a frontier model plan; restart from the plan. It is a failure of the spec, not of the code.

rows.title: Failure: `dragonfly gen` refuses to write
rows.summary: Before writing anything a generator refuses: a field type nobody declared, a name another file already declares, a source the platform has no pieces for, or a use case to wire that the project does not declare. It says which; nothing was written.
body: **Looks like.** `Character is already declared in <file>: remove or rename it, or generate another name`, `the type Origin is not declared`, `a database resource takes columns of basic types; a relation to Author is written by hand`.
**Next step.**
- A name already declared: the resource exists (`dragonfly gen inspect`); use it, choose another name, or remove the leftover file of an earlier attempt.
- A type not declared: generate that model first, or let `--from-json` find the nested models.
- A relation in a database resource: generate the resource with its basic columns, then add the relation by hand (`@manyToOne` and its `<name>Id` column).
- A source the platform lacks: mobile and web read APIs (`--source rest`); a database resource is for the backend.

- `<Name> is not declared` (`gen usecase`): write the use case first, at the place the message gives, then run the command again to wire it; or pass `--calls <Repository>.<method>` when all it does is call a repository.
- `the route names {x}, which the use case does not take`: a `{name}` of `--route` must be a parameter of the use case's `exec`.
- `the <platform> platform has no routes`: `--route` is for the backend; on mobile and web a screen calls the facade's alias.
- See first what it would write: `--dry-run`.

rows.title: Failure: the target's analyzer rejects the generated code
rows.summary: `nuclear check` reports nothing but the target's analyzer or the run complains inside `build/`. Never fix it there. The usual cause is a value without a type in the `.nuc`; otherwise it is a bug of the dialect to report.
body: **Looks like.** An error whose file is under `build/`, from the target's analyzer or at run time.

**Next step.** `dragonfly explain` gives the `.nuc` lines. Declare the type of the value at that line (`items: string[] = ...`); check that the call is awaited; rebuild. Still wrong with correct Nuclear: it is the dialect's bug; report the `.nuc` and the generated lines.

rows.title: Failure: the API answers 400, 404, 409 or 422
rows.summary: A backend written in Nuclear answers the status of its `Result` error: 422 an invalid body (a model's rule), 400 `Invalid`, 401 `Unauthorized`, 403 `Forbidden`, 404 `NotFound`, 409 `Conflict`. It is the code working: send a valid request or expect that status in the test.
body: - 422: a field breaks a rule decorator of the model (`@minLength`, `@email`...). The answer names the field.
- 404: `find(id)` or `getOne()` found no row and the use case returned `NotFound`.
- 409: the use case returned `Conflict` (a repeated unique value).
In a test: `expect(found.error.status == 404)`.

rows.title: Failure: no space left on the device
rows.summary: A run, a build or the evaluation stops because the temporary folder or the disk is full. Builds of example projects and Flutter leave large temporary folders: free the space and retry from the failed step.
body: **Looks like.** `No space left on device`, a run whose files are cut short; or a run that stops at its first step, *Check the connections*, with `278 MB free in /tmp (at least 500 MB are needed: free some space there)`: the message names the folder that is full (the project's, or the temporary one, which on many systems is memory with a size of its own).

**Next step.** `df -h /tmp ~`; remove scratch projects and old temporary build folders (`flutter_tools.*`, `nuclear-lsp-*`, `nuclear-web-device-*` in the temporary folder); `nuclear-loop retry <run>`. A run checks the free disk before it starts, and the diagnoser names this kind of failure `disk`: no retry helps until space is freed.

rows.title: Failure: `nuclear-graph knowledge check` fails
rows.summary: The knowledge base is behind the working tree: a generated asset is not what the tree gives now, a hand-written row's source changed, a row is invalid, or the graph holds an older revision. Build, review, check and ingest.
body: - `stale: assets/<shelf>/<file>.json ...` → `nuclear-graph knowledge build`.
- `review: <id> was written from <source>, which changed` → read the change; update the row or `nuclear-graph knowledge review <id>`.
- `<shelf>/<id>: links to <other>, which no row has` → fix the link or add the row.
- `the graph holds revision N and the knowledge base is revision M` → `nuclear-graph ingest`.
- `<file>: no section of sections.toml claims it` → give the new document a section in `sections.toml`.

rows.title: Failure: the request names nothing the project declares
rows.summary: Which declaration is it? A change, a rename or a fix of something that exists must name it as the project declares it (`Order`, `CancelOrder`): none of the project's names is written in the request. `dragonfly gen inspect` lists them.
body: **Looks like.** The analysis of a run stops with this question; no file was written.

**Cause.** The strategy of the request (`strategy:member`, `strategy:refactor-rename`, `strategy:data-migration`...) starts in the file that declares what changes, and the request names no declaration of the project: the name is misspelled, is a field or a method (only declarations are looked up), or is not in this project.
**Next step.** Write the declaration's name in the request as the project writes it, then run it again. A field or a method is renamed by hand: the compiler then names every use.

rows.title: Failure: the request lacks a fact its strategy cannot start without
rows.summary: A run stops at its analysis when the request does not say something nobody may guess: the fields of a resource, the url of an API, the two names of a rename, what should happen instead. The step lists the questions; answer them in the spec and run it again.
body: **Looks like.** `the request does not say: ...` at the Analysis step of the Specification stage; nothing was generated or written.

**Cause.** Each strategy names the facts it needs (`data.needs` of its row). The analyst looks for each one in the request (a `Key | Type` table, `name:type` pairs, an example answer, a url, `should`...) and asks for the ones it does not find. Agents never invent a field, a rule or a name.
**Next step.** Add the answer to the spec's description, then `nuclear-loop retry <run> --from spec`. The strategy is wrong for the request: name the right one in the spec (`- Strategy: usecase`).
